READABILITY.evidence: The new types in consistent_hash_types.go have clear names (ConsistentHashHeader, ConsistentHashCookieAttribute) and every field has a doc comment. The plugin helpers have readable names (hashPolicies, applyConsistentHash, newSourceIPHashPolicy) and follow the repo style.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: Follows the plugin pattern: an API type, a separate consistent_hash.go for IR and apply, and a merge function registered in MergeTrafficPolicies. Deepcopy and CRD come from `make go-generate-apis`. No debug leftovers are visible, and the diff shows no oversized files.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: The CRD has MinLength/MaxLength/MaxItems bounds and a CEL rule for ttl. A bad cookie TTL becomes a policy error and a bad regex fails Validate(). No errors are swallowed.

C7-11-CASE1.evidence: The merge unions lists with the higher-priority policy first, then dedupes and re-sorts. sourceIp comes from the higher-priority policy, and disable blocks lower-priority entries. Origins are recorded as `consistentHash`, and the merge golden output shows X-Shared, x-a, x-b, cookie, queryParameter. One quirk: `{}` gets its default sourceIp before merging, so it carries into the merged result.

C7-11-CASE2.evidence: The golden output shows `{}` producing a single connectionProperties sourceIp entry, and a rule-level disable removing the inherited x-route-hash. The CEL rule "no other fields may be set when disable is true" appears in the generated CRD YAML.
